title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
summary: Fixed context windows limit LLMs in long conversations and large-document analysis. MemGPT borrows the OS idea of hierarchical memory, letting the LLM page information between a bounded in-context store and external storage tiers, and uses interrupts to manage control flow with the user. The authors evaluate it on document analysis beyond the context window and on multi-session chat where agents retain and evolve memory over long interactions.
relevance: Externalizing agent state into explicit memory tiers is a prerequisite for packaging that state into a portable context and resuming an agent elsewhere.
notes: No peer-reviewed version found on OpenReview/Crossref; cited as arXiv preprint. The project later continued as Letta.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '23)
summary: The paper builds LLM-driven agents that simulate believable human behaviour in an interactive sandbox town of 25 agents. Each agent keeps a natural-language memory stream of its experiences, periodically synthesizes it into higher-level reflections, and retrieves relevant memories to plan. Ablations show that observation, planning and reflection each contribute substantially to believability, and the agents exhibit emergent coordinated social behaviour.
relevance: The memory-stream plus reflection design is a canonical model of long-lived agent state that any portable context or handoff envelope must capture or summarize.
search_query: Crossref query.bibliographic 'Generative Agents Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior'
notes: Crossref lists second author as 'Joseph O'Brien' and third as 'Carrie Jun Cai'; arXiv lists 'Joseph C. O'Brien' and 'Carrie J. Cai'.

title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model-based Agents
venue: ACM Transactions on Information Systems, vol. 43, no. 6
summary: This survey consolidates scattered work on memory in LLM-based agents. It discusses what agent memory is and why agents need it, reviews how memory modules are designed and evaluated, catalogues applications in which memory is central, and identifies limitations and future directions.
relevance: Provides a taxonomy of agent memory sources, forms and operations that can be used to define which state a portable task context must carry across agents.
search_query: Crossref query.bibliographic 'A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model based Agents'
notes: Author order differs between the TOIS version (Quanyu Dai second) and arXiv v1 (Dai sixth); the TOIS order from Crossref is used.

title: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025)
summary: Existing agent memory systems offer basic storage and retrieval with fixed structures and operations. A-Mem lets the agent organize memory itself following Zettelkasten principles: each new memory becomes a structured note with context, keywords and tags, is linked to related past notes, and can trigger updates to existing notes so the memory network evolves. Experiments across six foundation models report improvements over prior state-of-the-art baselines.
relevance: Self-organizing, linked memory is a candidate format for agent state that must remain coherent when transferred or merged between agents.
search_query: arXiv id_list 2502.12110; OpenReview search 'A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents'
notes: NeurIPS 2025 acceptance confirmed via arXiv journal comment and OpenReview (venue 'NeurIPS 2025 poster', note FiM0M8gcct). Proceedings title uses 'A-Mem'; arXiv uses 'A-MEM'. No DOI. date_published approximates the conference month.

title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
venue: ECAI 2025 (Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications)
summary: Mem0 is a memory architecture that dynamically extracts, consolidates and retrieves salient facts from ongoing conversations, with a variant that stores memories as a graph to capture relations. On the LOCOMO benchmark it is compared against memory-augmented systems, RAG configurations, full-context prompting and commercial memory offerings, and the authors report higher accuracy along with much lower latency and token cost than full-context processing.
relevance: Shows that persistent, externalized memory can be a service decoupled from any single model or session, which is what lets context survive movement between agents and runtimes.
search_query: Crossref query.bibliographic 'Mem0 Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory'
notes: Crossref types the record as a book-chapter in the IOS Press FAIA series; it is the ECAI 2025 proceedings paper.

title: DBOS: A DBMS-oriented Operating System
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, vol. 15, no. 1, pp. 21-30
summary: The authors argue that a distributed transactional DBMS, rather than a single-node OS plus separate cluster services, should be the foundation of a scalable cluster operating system. Their DBOS prototype implements scheduling, file management and inter-process communication as database operations with competitive performance, while gaining better analytics, less code, and transactions and high availability implemented once.
relevance: Putting all execution state in a transactional database is the basis of the durable-execution approach that lets workflows, including agent workflows, resume on another machine after failure.
search_query: Crossref query.bibliographic 'DBOS A DBMS-oriented Operating System'
notes: Crossref stores the title only as 'DBOS'; the full title is taken from the paper. PVLDB vol. 15 is dated 2021-09 by Crossref and is associated with VLDB 2022. Concerns durable state management in general, not LLM agents specifically.

title: Halfmoon: Log-Optimal Fault-Tolerant Stateful Serverless Computing
venue: Proceedings of the 29th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles (SOSP '23)
summary: Retrying failed serverless functions can apply duplicate updates to shared external state, and current log-based fixes for exactly-once semantics log every read and write. Halfmoon shows that logging only reads or only writes suffices, and gives two protocols that it proves are log-optimal, with a criterion and a pauseless mechanism for switching between them. The prototype reports lower latency and lower logging overhead than the prior system Boki.
relevance: Exactly-once handling of side effects on retry is the core correctness problem when an agent run is resumed or replayed on a different worker after a crash.
search_query: Crossref query.bibliographic 'Fault-tolerant and transactional stateful serverless workflows'
notes: Abstract read via Semantic Scholar (DOI lookup). Concerns serverless functions in general, not LLM agents specifically.

title: Parrot: Efficient Serving of LLM-based Applications with Semantic Variable
venue: 18th USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation (OSDI 24)
summary: LLM applications and agents chain many LLM requests, but public LLM services only see individual requests and optimize them blindly. Parrot introduces the Semantic Variable, an annotation on prompt inputs and outputs that exposes the data pipeline across requests so the service can run data-flow analysis and optimize end to end. Evaluations report up to an order-of-magnitude improvement on practical LLM application workloads.
relevance: Making inter-request state and dependencies explicit to the serving layer is a step toward serving infrastructure that can track and place agent state across machines.
search_query: arXiv id_list 2405.19888; USENIX OSDI '24 presentation page
notes: USENIX proceedings carry no DOI. date_published approximates the OSDI 2024 conference month.

title: Autellix: An Efficient Serving Engine for LLM Agents as General Programs
summary: Agentic programs issue many dependent LLM calls, but serving engines treat calls independently and suffer head-of-line blocking at both the request and program level. Autellix intercepts the calls, gives the scheduler program-level context, and introduces scheduling algorithms for single-threaded and distributed programs that preempt and prioritize calls based on the program's completed work. The authors report 4-15x higher program throughput at equal latency compared with systems such as vLLM.
relevance: Treating an agent program, rather than an individual call, as the unit the serving layer tracks and places across engines is directly relevant to relocating agent execution between machines.
notes: No peer-reviewed version found on OpenReview or Crossref as of the access date.

title: AIOS: LLM Agent Operating System
summary: Agents that access LLMs and tools without resource management can waste or misuse resources and cannot run concurrently efficiently. AIOS moves LLM and tool services into a kernel that offers scheduling, context management, memory and storage management and access control to agents, with an SDK for agents built in different frameworks. The authors report up to 2.1x faster execution when serving agents from several frameworks.
relevance: A kernel-level context manager that can save and restore agent context and serve agents from multiple frameworks is a concrete substrate for suspending, relocating and migrating agent runs.
search_query: arXiv id_list 2403.16971; OpenReview search 'AIOS: LLM Agent Operating System'
notes: COLM 2025 acceptance confirmed via arXiv comment and OpenReview (note L4HHkCDz2x). Author order follows the COLM/OpenReview record; arXiv v5 swaps Wenyue Hua and Mingyu Jin. No DOI. date_published approximates the conference month.

title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
summary: Long-horizon agents accumulate unbounded histories that raise inference memory cost and degrade reasoning. ACON compresses both observations and interaction history by iteratively refining natural-language compression guidelines from analysis of agent failures, without fine-tuning the agent, and then distils the compressor into smaller models. On AppWorld, OfficeBench and multi-objective QA it reduces peak token usage by 26-54% while improving task success over compression baselines.
relevance: Compressing agent history while preserving critical state is exactly the problem of producing a compact, transferable task context for handoff or resumption.
search_query: arXiv id_list 2510.00615; OpenReview search 'ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents'
notes: ICML 2026 acceptance confirmed via arXiv comment and OpenReview (venue 'ICML 2026 regular'). No DOI. date_published approximates the conference month.

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
summary: Adapting LLM applications by rewriting their contexts suffers from brevity bias and from context collapse, where repeated rewriting erodes detail. ACE treats contexts as evolving playbooks maintained through generation, reflection and curation, applying structured incremental updates instead of full rewrites. It improves over strong baselines on agent and finance benchmarks in both offline (system prompt) and online (agent memory) settings while lowering adaptation latency and cost, and can learn from execution feedback without labels.
relevance: Treats the agent's context as a structured, incrementally updated artifact, which is the form a portable task context needs in order to be carried and extended by successive agents.
search_query: arXiv id_list 2510.04618; OpenReview search 'Agentic Context Engineering'
notes: ICLR 2026 acceptance confirmed via arXiv comment and OpenReview (venue 'ICLR 2026 Poster'). No DOI. date_published approximates the conference month.

title: Get Experience from Practice: LLM Agents with Record & Replay
summary: The paper argues that LLM uncertainty and cost create reliability, privacy, cost and performance problems for agents, and proposes AgentRR, which brings classical record-and-replay into agent frameworks. Agents record their interaction traces and decisions, summarize them into structured multi-level experiences, and replay those experiences on similar tasks, with check functions acting as a trust anchor for safety during replay. It outlines application modes such as user demonstrations, large-small model collaboration and privacy-aware execution, and envisions a shared experience repository.
relevance: Recorded agent traces that can be summarized and replayed elsewhere connect reproducibility, auditability and transfer of agent work between models and machines.

notes: Primarily a paradigm/design paper; the abstract does not report quantitative results. No peer-reviewed version found.
